subject: Clarify: incident notice handoff, scope definitions, and subprocessor cooperation
messages:
From: Samantha Li <samantha.li@clearfin.com>
To: aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Legal (ClearFin) <legal@clearfin.com>
Date: Fri, 05 Jul 2025 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on DPA incident clauses and subprocessor handoff

Hi Aditya,

Thanks again for the walkthrough earlier. Our legal team reviewed Redwood's standard DPA language and had a few follow-ups specifically around incident notice and evidence handoff:

- The current clause requires "prompt notice" — can you confirm whether Redwood interprets that as 48 or 72 hours from detection? We need a firm window for our Board.
- What does Redwood consider "affected data"? Is this limited to customer-controlled inputs, or does it include derived telemetry, logs, and cached KV entries?
- If a subprocessor (e.g., telemetry vendor) is implicated, what is Redwood's process for engaging that subprocessor and sharing evidence with ClearFin? Do you expect direct disclosures or that Redwood will act as a broker?
- For cross-border forensic handoff, do you provide hashes and manifest files only, or can we request encrypted transfer of a snapshot?

Attached is a short list of the edits our counsel proposes. We're hopeful we can agree without a lengthy redline. Can your legal or ops folks confirm the concrete timelines and technical handoff options?

Best,
Samantha
Director, Security Operations
ClearFin Inc.

Attachment: ClearFin_DPA_incident_questions_v1.pdf (pdf)

From: aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Li <samantha.li@clearfin.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 05 Jul 2025 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on DPA incident clauses and subprocessor handoff

Hi Samantha — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers up-front, then I’ll loop in Marissa (contracts) and Kim (privacy/infra) for the technical specifics: 

1) Notice window: Our standard practice is to provide initial customer notification within 48 hours of detection for incidents that meet the "notifiable" threshold (see below). We typically follow up with a 72-hour status update and a 7-day preliminary report. We can accept 72h as a contractual commitment if ClearFin requires it, but our ops target is 48h for higher-severity incidents.

2) "Affected data" scope: We classify "affected data" as: (a) customer-submitted inputs and outputs stored in the model KV/cache or persistent storage tied to the customer tenant, and (b) any persisted backups or exported artifacts that contain customer identifiers. Telemetry/usage logs that are strictly aggregated and anonymized are out of scope. Non-persisted inference caches (ephemeral KV) are treated as transient unless a snapshot was taken and stored. We can add precise examples to the DPA to avoid ambiguity.

3) Subprocessor engagement: Redwood will act as the primary point of contact and will coordinate engagement with downstream subprocessors. We will not require customers to sign separate NDAs with subprocessors — Redwood will broker evidence requests. If ClearFin requests direct engagement, we can facilitate it under a documented access process and limited-scope NDA. We do require subprocessors to follow our incident handling SLA and evidence preservation obligations.

4) Forensic handoff options: We provide a standard manifest and SHA256 hashes for exported artifacts. For high-sensitivity cases we support secure, encrypted transfer (SFTP or customer-managed GCS bucket with customer-side key). If regulatory or legal process requires physical transfer, we will coordinate with legal/forensics and provide chain-of-custody documentation.

I’ve attached a draft redline I started (basic language) and flagged where we need Marissa/Kim to confirm legal wording and export mechanics. Next: Marissa, can you give contractual language for 48h vs 72h and the acceptance criteria for what constitutes a "notifiable incident"? Kim — could you outline the methods and typical ETA for producing a manifest and encrypted snapshot?

Thanks,
Aditya
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redline_incident_clause_aditya_v2.docx (docx)

From: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Samantha Li <samantha.li@clearfin.com>
Cc: kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 05 Jul 2025 10:32:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on DPA incident clauses and subprocessor handoff

Hi all,

Adding a legal read. High level positions below — I’ll attach a clean redline after internal review:

- Timing: We are comfortable with contract language that says "initial notice within 72 hours of Redwood's confirmed detection" with an operational commitment (SLA note) that we aim for 48 hours for P0/P1 incidents. The reason: legal needs the 72h cushion to account for triage false positives and confirmation.

- Notifiable incident: propose a definition clause: "an incident that results in unauthorized access, exfiltration, or disclosure of Customer Data as defined in Section X, excluding aggregated telemetry and system health logs that do not contain Customer Data." This keeps telemetry out of scope unless it contains tenant-identifiable data.

- Subprocessor cooperation: Redwood will coordinate evidence requests and, upon Customer request and a documented lawful basis, may provide access to subprocessor-produced artifacts. We propose an "assistance clause" that obligates Redwood to use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain materials from subprocessors within 10 business days of a validated request; exceptions for legal holds and export restrictions should be called out.

- Evidence format & delivery: standard manifest (CSV), SHA256 hashes, and a persistent export (tar.gz). Support encrypted transfer to a customer-managed bucket; timeline: typical manifest within 48h of the initial notice, full export within 7–14 business days depending on scope. We’ll flag costs for unusually large exports.

Kim, please confirm the 48h manifest ETA is achievable from infra ops for tenant-scoped incidents and what gating we should add (e.g., forensic snapshot scheduling, compute availability).

Marissa
Staff Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Samantha Li <samantha.li@clearfin.com>
Date: Fri, 05 Jul 2025 12:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on DPA incident clauses and subprocessor handoff

Thanks — quick ops confirmation from infra:

- Manifest ETA: For a tenant-scoped incident where we can identify impacted shards/indices, we can produce a manifest (list of files, object keys, and SHA256 hashes) within 24–48 hours. If containment work or live-forensics is required, initial manifest may be limited and supplemented later.
- Full export: Typical window 5–10 business days; complex cross-region cases that require legal export reviews may extend to 15 business days. We’ll provide interim status updates.
- Subprocessor evidence: We have contractual SLAs with critical subprocessors (telemetry, vector-db host) to preserve forensic snapshots for 30 days upon request; obtaining artifacts from third parties often adds 3–7 business days.
- Transfer methods: SFTP with customer public key, customer-managed GCS/Azure bucket (object ACL + signed URL), or encrypted tarball via a temporary secure transfer service. We prefer customer-managed bucket for speed.

Operational caveats: if data sampling is required to avoid exporting PII not in scope, we’ll propose sampling and provide hash lists for full verification. Any expedited requests that require emergency support will be scoped and may include an engineering time-and-materials estimate.

Kim
Director, Privacy & Infrastructure
